member.name: T:Ffmpegkit.Droid.FFmpegKitEnumExtensions
member.summary: Converts FFmpegKit's Java enums into managed enums.
member.remarks: and are real Java enums, so the binding projects them as subclasses rather than C# enums. They must stay that way — the Java objects are what get passed back across JNI — but as a result they cannot be used in a switch, and comparing them with == compares managed peer references, which are not guaranteed to be the same instance for the same Java constant. Converting once at the boundary avoids both problems.

member.name: M:Ffmpegkit.Droid.FFmpegKit.ExecuteAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Runs an FFmpeg command and awaits its completion.
member.param: The FFmpeg command, as it would be typed after ffmpeg.
Cancels the running session.
member.returns: The completed session. Inspect for the outcome.
member.remarks:
The synchronous blocks the calling thread for the whole transcode, which on the UI thread means a frozen app. This wraps FFmpegKit's own asynchronous path so the command can simply be awaited.
A failing command completes the task normally with a non-success return code; it does not throw. Cancellation asks FFmpeg to stop, and the session then completes with a cancelled return code rather than raising — FFmpeg may still have written a partial output file.

member.name: M:Ffmpegkit.Droid.FFmpegKitConfig.GetSafParameterForRead(Android.Net.Uri)
member.summary: Turns a content:// URI into a path FFmpeg can read from.
member.param: A URI obtained from the photo picker, a document picker, or a share intent.
member.returns: A path to pass to FFmpeg in place of a file name.
member.remarks:
On Android 10 and later an app cannot open arbitrary file paths, and anything the user picks arrives as a content:// URI. FFmpeg has no idea what those are, so passing one straight into a command fails to open the input. This registers the URI with FFmpegKit and hands back a path that resolves through the Storage Access Framework:
var input = FFmpegKitConfig.GetSafParameterForRead(pickedUri); var session = await FFmpegKit.ExecuteAsync($"-i {input} -c:v mpeg4 \"{outputPath}\"");
Note the returned value is already a complete argument and must not be quoted.
The registration lives as long as the process, so treat these as per-operation rather than obtaining one for every item in a long list.
Overload of that uses the application context, since callers rarely have a reason to pass another.

member.name: M:Ffmpegkit.Droid.FFmpegKitConfig.GetSafParameterForWrite(Android.Net.Uri)
member.summary: Turns a content:// URI into a path FFmpeg can write to.
member.remarks: The document must already exist - the Storage Access Framework has no notion of FFmpeg creating a file - so create it first with ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT and pass the resulting URI here. See for the rest of the caveats.

member.name: T:Ffmpegkit.Droid.MediaValues
member.summary: Parsing for the values FFprobe reports as strings.
member.remarks: FFprobe emits numbers in a fixed, invariant format - "12.345000", "30/1" - and always with a dot as the decimal separator. Parsing them with the ambient culture is wrong and quietly so: on a German device double.Parse("12.345000") returns 12,345,000 because the dot reads as a group separator, and on a French one it throws. Everything here parses invariantly, and returns null rather than throwing when a value is absent or unparseable - FFprobe omits fields routinely depending on the container.
